finalText:
**Merge** ties two branches together with a new commit that says "these branches came together here." You keep both histories intact. It's safe because nobody's past commits change.

**Rebase** replays your commits on top of the other branch, as if you had started from a different point. It rewrites your commit history to make a cleaner line.

**Use merge when:**
- You're pulling a feature branch into main or a shared branch
- Multiple people are working on the same branch
- You want a clear record of when branches joined

**Use rebase when:**
- You're cleaning up your own branch before pushing it out
- You want a straight-line history that's easier to follow
- Only you are working on that branch

The golden rule: **rebase on your own work, merge on shared branches.** Rebasing rewrites commits, so if someone else is also on that branch, their copy of the history breaks. Merge is safe because it only adds a new commit — everyone's old commits stay as they were.

For a feature branch you're working on solo, rebase keeps things tidy. For main or anything multiple people touch, merge is the safer play.
